summary: R5-NEW-MAJ-001 (§1 conditional carve-out) is CLOSED — §1 item 2(b) now explicitly conditions the log-entry on cascade-status being onboarded or onboarded-operator-bump and states blocked-on-adopter-conflict slices MUST NOT modify the log file. R5-NEW-MAJ-002 (safety — meaningful-content format spec) is PARTIALLY CLOSED: a regex is present and the 3 worked examples in the plan-doc all behave correctly. However, the regex contains a material prose/spec inconsistency (new MAJ-001), and the §6 024B acceptance criteria have not been updated to reference the invariant 2 regex spec (new MAJ-002), and the CI script's fail-closed behavior on an absent or unrecognised cascade-status field is unspecified (new MAJ-003). R6 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle) is not met.

findings.title: R5-NEW-MAJ-002 partial closure verification: regex format spec present at invariant 2 with 3 worked examples — PRESENT but contains a prose/regex inconsistency (see R6-NEW-MAJ-001)

findings.title: Regex test — 3 plan-doc worked examples
findings.evidence: Example 1 (✅): '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123 at 024C; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort.' — Regex walk: '^- ' matches '- '; '\*\*TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-' matches '**TF-024X-renovate-'; '[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+' matches 'jrnb2024-pim' (first segment 'jrnb2024', one (?:-[a-z0-9]+) repetition '-pim'); '\*\*' matches '**'; ' \(' matches ' ('; '(open|pending|in-progress|closed)' matches 'open'; '\): ' matches '): '; '.{20,}' matches well-over-20 chars; '$' satisfied. PASSES — correct. Example 2 (❌): '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim**' — After '\*\*' the regex requires ' \(' but the string ends; FAILS — correct. Example 3 (❌): '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):' — After '): ' the regex requires '.{20,}' but zero chars remain; FAILS — correct.
findings.outcome: All 3 plan-doc examples behave as specified

findings.title: Regex test — 5 additional edge cases
findings.evidence: Edge case 1 (status field with extra whitespace): '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim**  (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123; track until adopter enables Renovate.' — The regex requires exactly one space before '\(' via '\*\* \('. Two spaces ('  (') causes FAIL. This is not a false-positive concern: the format spec enforces exactly one space, and a correctly-formatted entry would have exactly one space. The spec prose (line 55) confirms 'then a parenthesised status field' implicitly requires the single-space separator. No bypass surface. Edge case 2 (description exactly 19 chars): '- **TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-ct** (pending): conflict_1234567890' where 'conflict_1234567890' is 19 chars — FAILS because '.{20,}' requires ≥20. Correct. Edge case 3 (slug with uppercase): '- **TF-024X-renovate-JrnB2024-PIM** (open): Renovate disabled; this is a long description of the state.' — '[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+' requires lowercase; uppercase letters cause FAIL. Correct — spec says 'adopter-slug is <owner>-<repo> lowercased'. Edge case 4 (no list-marker prefix): '**TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort here.' — '^- ' requires the line to start with '- '; without it, FAILS. Correct. Edge case 5 (all-whitespace description — BYPASS): '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):                      ' (20+ spaces as description) — '.{20,}' counts ALL characters including whitespace; 20 spaces = 20 chars = .{20,} PASSES. The prose spec (line 55) says '≥20 non-whitespace characters of description' but the regex '.{20,}' counts whitespace. An all-whitespace description PASSES the regex but FAILS the prose spec. This is a material inconsistency creating a bypass surface — see R6-NEW-MAJ-001.
findings.outcome: 4 of 5 edge cases behave correctly; edge case 5 reveals a prose/regex inconsistency — new MAJ filed

findings.title: Regex .{20,} counts whitespace but prose spec says '≥20 non-whitespace characters' — all-whitespace descriptions bypass the meaningful-content gate
findings.evidence: Invariant 2's meaningful-content format spec (plan-doc line 52–55) contains two conflicting specifications of the description requirement: (A) The REGEX uses '.{20,}$' — where '.' matches any character including spaces and tabs. A description of 20+ spaces satisfies '.{20,}$'. (B) The PROSE (line 55) says 'then ≥20 non-whitespace characters of description.' A description of 20 spaces has 0 non-whitespace characters and fails this requirement. The two specifications produce different outcomes on the same input: '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):                      ' (exactly 20 spaces as description) — PASSES the regex, FAILS the prose. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh against the regex literally (which is the spec's intent — 'Codex executors implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh use this regex literally' per line 55) would allow an all-whitespace description to pass CI. This re-opens the stub-row bypass surface in a narrow but real way: an executor can write a TF row with 20 spaces of description, pass the regex check, and produce a row with no meaningful content. The bypass is narrower than the pre-fix state (must include a valid prefix + valid status value + at least 20 chars) but still allows the description portion to carry zero information. Fix required: align the regex and prose. Option A: change the regex to use '\S.{18,}\S' or '(?=.*\S{3,}).{20,}' or '\S.{0,}(?:.|\n){17,}' — simplest readable fix is '\S.*' with a separate check for ≥20 total chars and starts with non-whitespace; practically, replace '.{20,}' with '\S\S?.{18,}' which requires the description to start with at least 1 non-whitespace character within the first 2 chars and have ≥20 total (this is weaker than 'all non-whitespace' but much stronger than all-whitespace). Option B: keep the regex as-is and remove the '≥20 non-whitespace characters' language from the prose, replacing it with '≥20 characters (whitespace-inclusive; the dot in .{20,} counts all characters)' — this weakens the spec but eliminates the inconsistency. Option A is the correct fix because the intent is clearly to require meaningful text, not whitespace padding. The minimal unambiguous fix: replace '.{20,}' in the regex with '\S.{19,}' (requires description to start with a non-whitespace character, then at least 19 more characters of any kind — total ≥20 chars, first char non-whitespace). This is still implementable literally by check-invocation-log-entry.sh. The prose '≥20 non-whitespace characters' should then be updated to match the new regex semantics ('description starts with a non-whitespace character and is ≥20 characters total').
findings.recommendation: Replace '.{20,}' in the invariant 2 regex with '\S.{19,}' and update the prose on line 55 from '≥20 non-whitespace characters of description' to 'description starting with a non-whitespace character and ≥20 characters total'. Propagate to any site that quotes the regex or the .{20,} description floor (R-024-06, R-024-07, §6 024B acceptance criteria). This is a 1-line regex change + 2–3 prose updates.

findings.title: §6 024B acceptance criteria still says 'non-empty description' for onboarded-operator-bump path — not updated to reference invariant 2 regex spec; propagation gap creates implementation-ambiguous floor
findings.evidence: §6 slice plan table, 024B row (plan-doc line 201): 'for onboarded-operator-bump: requires log entry + target match + TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug> STATUS.md row with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; rejects bare-prefix stubs)' — this still says 'status field + non-empty description' not 'format per invariant 2 regex spec'. The invariant 2 fix-round-5 format spec block established the regex (.{20,}) + ≥20-char floor as the normative machine-enforceable spec, but the §6 024B acceptance criterion was not updated to reference it. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh and reading §6 as their acceptance criterion (which they will — §6 is the slice deliverable specification and acceptance gate) would implement 'non-empty description' (any single character) rather than 'format per invariant 2 regex (≥20 chars; precise format spec).' This is the same propagation-gap class that produced R5-NEW-MAJ-001 (§1 propagation), R5-NEW-MAJ-001 correctness (§3 propagation), R5-NEW-MAJ-002 completeness (§5.2 propagation), and R5-NEW-MAJ-002 completeness (R-024-06 propagation) in prior rounds. §6 is the MOST IMPORTANT propagation site for a Codex executor: it is the normative acceptance specification that check-invocation-log-entry.sh is implemented against. If §6 still says 'non-empty description' while invariant 2 says '.{20,}' and the prose says '≥20 non-whitespace characters', the 024B implementer has three inconsistent specs. The weakest spec ('non-empty description') would rationally win because it's the acceptance test. The regex protection reverts to 'any non-empty string' — which is weaker than the intent and almost as weak as the pre-R4 state (prefix-string containment only, before meaningful-content was added). Fix required: update the §6 024B acceptance criteria for both the onboarded-operator-bump path (TF-024X-renovate row) and the blocked-on-adopter-conflict path (TF-024X-conflict row) to say 'with meaningful content per invariant 2's regex spec' or simply 'format-per-invariant-2-regex'. Also check whether the §6 024B note about 'closes 024A R1 MAJ-SAFE-001 ...' in the acceptance text should also reference R5-NEW-MAJ-002.
findings.recommendation: In §6 024B acceptance criteria (line 201): change 'meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; rejects bare-prefix stubs)' to 'meaningful content per invariant 2's format-spec regex (status field ∈ enumerated set; description ≥20 chars starting with non-whitespace; rejects bare-prefix stubs and whitespace-only descriptions)' at both the onboarded-operator-bump occurrence and the blocked-on-adopter-conflict occurrence. Confirm the closes marker at the end of the 024B row also references R5-NEW-MAJ-002 (safety).

findings.title: CI script fail-open vs fail-closed behavior on absent/unrecognised cascade-status field is unspecified — absent field bypasses all of invariant 2's enforcement
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 (plan-doc line 44) describes check-invocation-log-entry.sh as a script that 'parses DISPATCH-NOTE cascade-status: field (one of three values: onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict) and applies the appropriate check-path.' The spec does not state what the script does when (a) the cascade-status: field is absent from DISPATCH-NOTE, (b) the field is present but contains an unrecognised value (e.g. 'pending', 'onboarded_operator_bump' with underscore instead of hyphen, 'ONBOARDED' in uppercase, or a fourth value not in the enumeration), or (c) the DISPATCH-NOTE file itself is absent from the PR. The §6 024B acceptance criteria (line 201) also does not specify this behavior: it says 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh parses DISPATCH-NOTE cascade-status: field and enforces all three close-states' for the three named values, but is silent on the absent/unrecognised case. If the CI script exits 0 (pass) on parse failure or absent field, then a cascade slice PR that simply lacks the cascade-status: field in DISPATCH-NOTE bypasses ALL three enforcement paths. This is a complete invariant 2 bypass: no log-entry check, no TF-reference check, no negative log-file-unmodified assertion. The missing-field case is the highest-severity bypass surface in the entire invariant 2 spec because it requires only omission, not a crafted exploit. A similar class of under-specification (what happens when the enumeration is incomplete) was addressed at R3 (R3-NEW-MAJ-001 correctness — the third cascade-status value was missing). This finding extends that class to the absent/unrecognised-value case. The spec states only the three enumerated paths' behavior; a fourth implicit path (absent/unknown) has no specified behavior. Fix required: add a fourth path to invariant 2: 'cascade-status: field absent or unrecognised value → CI FAILS with a specific error message naming the expected values. check-invocation-log-entry.sh MUST exit non-zero on absent or unrecognised cascade-status (fail-closed, not fail-open).' Also add to §6 024B acceptance criteria: the CI script MUST exit non-zero when cascade-status: is absent or not one of {onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict}.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit fail-closed spec to invariant 2: after the three-path enumeration, add a fourth path: 'cascade-status: absent or unrecognised value (any value not in {onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict}): CI MUST exit non-zero (fail-closed) — check-invocation-log-entry.sh treats unrecognised cascade-status as a hard error, not a no-op.' Propagate to §6 024B acceptance criteria: add 'unrecognised or absent cascade-status: field causes check-invocation-log-entry.sh to exit non-zero' to the 024B acceptance test list. Propagate to R-024-06 if it enumerates the CI check paths. This is the missing fourth branch in the three-path enumeration.

findings.title: Scan for other positive-evidence-only carve-outs lacking negative assertion treatment
findings.evidence: Full scan of the plan-doc for carve-out patterns: (1) Invariant 2 onboarded path ('PR MUST modify branch-protection-log.md AND the modified entry's target repo string MUST match') — two positive assertions, no negative. Already reviewed at R5 (R5-SCAN-ONBOARDED-PATH-NEGATIVE-ASSERTION) — no bypass here because the bypass incentive runs the other direction (an attacker would want to NOT modify the log, not modify it extra). The onboarded path's positive-only design is load-bearing. (2) Invariant 3 ('cascade does NOT touch existing adopter content') — this is a scope-limiter, not a CI-enforced assertion. No CI enforcement is claimed for it; it is policy. A cascade slice that violates invariant 3 would be caught at review (the adopter-side PR would show modifications to files other than the wrapper). Not a CI bypass surface. (3) §5.2 item 1 (adopter PR shape) — describes PR body contents (cost estimate, bus-factor disclosure, etc.) as requirements but there is no CI enforcement of PR body contents. This is an acceptance-reviewer dependency, not a bypass surface — the 3-lens R1 review covers the SCP-side cascade slice PR, not the adopter-side PR contents. No new CI bypass surface. (4) Threshold A criterion in §8: '≥3 of 5 cohort adopters have required-check live + ≥1 Renovate cycle propagated cleanly' — USER-GATE-E is a human gate signed by @jrnb2024. Threshold A is not CI-enforced; it is operator-signed. This is by design. Reviewer-dependence at Threshold A is appropriate for a gate that requires human judgment (checking Renovate PR URLs, observing clean CI runs). Not a CI bypass surface. (5) §5.2 item 2 blocked-on-adopter-conflict description — references 'meaningful content per invariant 2's regex spec' which is the correct cross-reference. The cross-reference is present. Consistent with invariant 2. (6) R-024-07 'with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description after the slug)' — still uses 'non-empty description' language (same propagation gap as §6, but R-024-07 also says 'per invariant 2' as a cross-reference which partially mitigates). The 'per invariant 2' cross-reference is present in R-024-07 so the regex spec applies. However, the local 'non-empty description' language contradicts the regex's ≥20-char floor — see R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (the regex itself has the whitespace inconsistency). No additional standalone bypass from R-024-07's 'non-empty description' because it explicitly defers to invariant 2. After R6-NEW-MAJ-001 is fixed at invariant 2, R-024-07 inherits the fix via the cross-reference. No separate fix needed at R-024-07 on this specific point.
findings.outcome: No additional positive-evidence-only carve-outs beyond the three new MAJ findings above

findings.title: R-024-06 meaningful-content reference post-fix-round-5 — consistent with invariant 2 regex spec
findings.evidence: R-024-06 mitigation (plan-doc line 219): 'CI enforcement (invariant 2): when cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict, check-invocation-log-entry.sh (a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE with meaningful content matching invariant 2's regex spec (status field + ≥20 char description; bare-prefix stubs fail CI) AND (b) actively asserts that docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in the PR diff. All three checks are required; positive evidence + meaningful-content format match + negative assertion.' The phrase 'with meaningful content matching invariant 2's regex spec' is the correct reference. This site correctly defers to invariant 2 for the format spec. Once R6-NEW-MAJ-001 is fixed at invariant 2 (aligning regex and prose), R-024-06 inherits the fix via the cross-reference. No standalone fix needed at R-024-06 beyond ensuring the invariant 2 fix propagates.
findings.outcome: R-024-06 correctly cross-references invariant 2 regex spec; no standalone bypass

r6_closures_verified: R5-NEW-MAJ-001: CLOSED (§1 item 2(b) conditional carve-out present); R5-NEW-MAJ-002 (safety — regex present): PARTIALLY CLOSED (regex is present and correctly catches the 3 plan-doc examples and 4 of 5 edge cases, but prose/regex inconsistency introduces new MAJ-001)
r6_verdict_rationale: R5's two safety closures are substantively addressed: R5-NEW-MAJ-001 (§1 propagation gap) is fully closed with explicit conditional language at §1 item 2(b). R5-NEW-MAJ-002 (format spec) has a regex present that correctly handles the plan-doc examples and most edge cases. However, three new MAJ findings surface: (1) R6-NEW-MAJ-001: the regex .{20,} counts whitespace characters, but the prose spec says '≥20 non-whitespace characters' — a 20-space description PASSES the regex, reopening the stub-row bypass in a narrow but real way. This is a prose/regex inconsistency at the normative spec level; the regex literal was supposed to be unambiguous but contradicts its own prose. Fix is a 1-line regex change. (2) R6-NEW-MAJ-002: §6 024B acceptance criteria still says 'status field + non-empty description' for both TF-row paths rather than 'per invariant 2 regex spec' — a Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh against §6 as their acceptance gate would implement the weaker 'non-empty description' spec, not the ≥20-char regex spec. This is the fifth consecutive round that surfaces a propagation gap in the meaningful-content chain. §6 is the highest-risk propagation site because it is the Codex executor's acceptance contract for 024B. (3) R6-NEW-MAJ-003: the CI script's behavior on absent or unrecognised cascade-status field values is completely unspecified. A cascade slice PR lacking the cascade-status: field entirely would bypass all of invariant 2's enforcement if the script fails-open on parse failure. The spec enumerates only the three named paths' behavior; the fourth implicit path (absent/unknown) is a complete bypass of the entire invariant 2 CI enforcement chain. This is a new class of finding not previously surfaced in R1–R5 and is not a propagation gap from prior rounds.
